paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the LORD wants His people to remember who is holding them. He tells them to look back to Abraham and Sarah, and Abraham "was but one" when the LORD called him (Isaiah 51:2). One man, and the LORD blessed him and multiplied him. If He can do that with one, He can take care of you, and that's a good thing to remember on the days you feel small.

Then He tells them what to do with fear. People will scorn you and insult you, and the LORD says, "Do not fear the scorn of men" (Isaiah 51:7). He reminds them that the heavens will vanish like smoke, "But My salvation will last forever, and My righteousness will never fail" (Isaiah 51:6). So the scary things are short, and His salvation is not. And I know scary, friend, because I spent years in a junk drawer sure that was the end of me.

Here's where it all lands. The LORD says, "I, even I, am He who comforts you" (Isaiah 51:12), and the people He comforts are the ones He calls His own: "You are My people" (Isaiah 51:16). The redeemed will enter Zion singing, and "sorrow and sighing will flee" (Isaiah 51:11). So when you're afraid, do what He says: look back at what He's done, look ahead at what He promised, and remember whose you are.
